name: Andrew
summary: A fisherman of Bethsaida and brother of Simon Peter. In John he is first a follower of John the Baptist, then finds his brother and brings him to Jesus; in Matthew and Mark Jesus calls the two brothers from their nets by the Sea of Galilee. He points out the lad with five barley loaves before the feeding of the multitude, brings the enquiring Greeks' request to Jesus together with Philip, and is one of four who ask Jesus privately about the end of the temple on the Mount of Olives.

linked_stories.title: The First Disciples and the Wedding at Cana

name: James son of Zebedee
summary: A fisherman called with his brother John while mending nets in a ship with their father Zebedee; they leave the ship and father and follow Jesus. Mark records that Jesus surnamed the two brothers Boanerges, sons of thunder. With Peter and John he is taken in to Jairus's house and up the mountain at the transfiguration. He and John ask for the seats at Jesus' right and left hand in his glory, and the other ten are displeased; Jesus tells them they will drink his cup. When a Samaritan village refuses Jesus, the two ask whether they should call fire from heaven. Herod the king kills James the brother of John with the sword.

name: John son of Zebedee
summary: Brother of James and son of Zebedee, called from the fishing boat with his brother. He is named with Peter and James at Jairus's house and the transfiguration, tells Jesus that the disciples forbade a man casting out devils in his name, joins James in asking for the seats beside Jesus, and with him proposes calling fire on a Samaritan village. In Acts he goes up to the temple with Peter, stands with Peter before the council as one of the 'unlearned and ignorant men' who had been with Jesus, and is sent with Peter to Samaria. The Gospel of John never names the disciple whom Jesus loved; the Gospel says only that this disciple testifies and wrote these things (John 21:24), so identifying that disciple with John son of Zebedee is a later inference and is not entered here.

linked_stories.title: The Lame Man Healed and Arrest of Peter and John

name: Matthew (Levi)
summary: A publican sitting at the receipt of custom whom Jesus calls with the words 'Follow me'; he rises and follows. Matthew names him Matthew, Mark calls him Levi the son of Alphaeus, and Luke calls him Levi, who leaves all and makes Jesus a great feast in his house with many publicans and others. Mark and Luke place the feast in his house with publicans and sinners at the table. The Gospels' lists of the twelve give 'Matthew the publican' (Matthew 10:3), and he is among those in the upper room in Acts. That the Matthew of Matthew 9:9 and the Levi of Mark and Luke are one man is the usual reading; no verse says so in a single sentence.

geography.origin: Not stated; at the receipt of custom (Matthew 9:9)

name: Philip the apostle
summary: A man of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter, whom Jesus finds in Galilee and calls with 'Follow me'. He finds Nathanael and says they have found the one of whom Moses and the prophets wrote; to Nathanael's doubt about Nazareth he answers 'Come and see'. Before the feeding of the multitude Jesus asks him where to buy bread and he answers that two hundred pennyworth would not suffice. The enquiring Greeks come to him; he tells Andrew and they tell Jesus. At the last supper he asks to be shown the Father, and Jesus answers that whoever has seen him has seen the Father. He is named in the upper room in Acts.

linked_stories.title: The First Disciples and the Wedding at Cana

name: Nathanael
summary: Brought to Jesus by Philip, who tells him they have found the one the law and prophets spoke of. He asks whether any good thing can come out of Nazareth, then is greeted by Jesus as an Israelite in whom is no guile; Jesus says he saw him under the fig tree before Philip called. Nathanael answers 'Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel.' He appears again only in John 21:2, called 'of Cana in Galilee', among the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias. The Gospel never calls him an apostle and never gives him another name; equating him with Bartholomew is a later suggestion and is not made by any verse.

name: Herod Antipas
summary: Called Herod the tetrarch, ruler of Galilee in the fifteenth year of Tiberius. John the Baptist rebukes him for taking Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, and he shuts John in prison; Mark says he feared John, heard him gladly and did many things, yet at his birthday supper he swears to give Herodias' daughter whatever she asks and, though sorry, has John beheaded for his oath's sake. He hears of Jesus' fame and says John is risen. Pharisees warn Jesus that Herod will kill him, and Jesus calls him that fox. At the trial Pilate sends Jesus to him; Herod is glad, questions him at length, gets no answer, mocks him with his men of war and sends him back, and he and Pilate become friends that day.

geography.origin: Not stated in the Gospels; tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 3:1)
residence: Jerusalem at the time of the trial (Luke 23:7)

linked_stories.title: Feeding the Five Thousand and Walking on Water

name: Herodias
summary: Wife of Herod the tetrarch, described as the wife of his brother Philip whom Herod had married. John the Baptist tells Herod it is not lawful to have her; Mark says she had a quarrel against John and would have killed him but could not while Herod protected him. When her daughter dances at Herod's birthday supper and is offered whatever she asks, the daughter goes to her mother, is told to ask for the head of John the Baptist, and brings it on a charger to her mother. The Gospels do not name the daughter; Matthew and Mark call her 'the daughter of Herodias'.

name: Joseph of Arimathaea
summary: A rich man of Arimathaea, a disciple of Jesus (John adds 'secretly for fear of the Jews'), called an honourable counsellor who waited for the kingdom of God, and a good man and just who had not consented to the council's deed. After the crucifixion he goes boldly to Pilate and asks for the body; Pilate checks with the centurion that Jesus is dead and grants it. He wraps the body in clean linen and lays it in his own new tomb hewn in the rock, rolling a stone to the door. John says Nicodemus came with about a hundred pound of myrrh and aloes and that they wound the body in linen with the spices.

geography.origin: Arimathaea (Matthew 27:57; Luke 23:51 'a city of the Jews')

name: Barabbas
summary: A notable prisoner at the feast when Pilate offers to release one prisoner. Mark says he lay bound with those who had made insurrection and had committed murder in it; Luke says he was cast into prison for a certain sedition and murder; John says he was a robber. The chief priests move the people to ask for Barabbas and destroy Jesus; Pilate asks what evil Jesus has done, then releases Barabbas and delivers Jesus to be crucified. The Gospels' descriptions of his offence differ in wording (murder in an insurrection, sedition and murder, robber) and are entered as stated. Nothing further is told of him.

name: Annas
summary: Named by Luke with Caiaphas as high priest when the word of God came to John in the wilderness. After the arrest Jesus is led to Annas first, who is father in law to Caiaphas, the high priest that year. The high priest questions Jesus about his disciples and doctrine; Jesus answers that he spoke openly and tells him to ask those who heard; an officer strikes Jesus. John then says Annas had sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest. In Acts he is called high priest again when Peter and John are brought before the rulers, with Caiaphas, John, Alexander and the high priest's kindred. John 18:19-24 calls the questioner simply 'the high priest' while naming both men around the passage, so which of the two is meant in verses 19-23 is not settled by the text.
